prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1082; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On the afternoon of the reported collision, officers were dispatched to a rear-end crash in Baytown, Texas. Driver 2 was stopped in the travel lane when the front of a vehicle operated by Driver 1 struck the rear of the stopped car. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Driver 1 reported a wrist injury and was evaluated at the scene, and the officer found the injury consistent with the force of the impact. A Passenger was also in Driver 1's vehicle and was confirmed as an occupant by both drivers and by independent witnesses who came forward. Witnesses described the sequence of events the same way Driver 2 did, and photographs taken at the scene show damage to the rear of Driver 2's vehicle and the front of Driver 1's vehicle that matches the reported impact. Officers found no indication of prior damage to either vehicle. Both drivers were cooperative, and the vehicles were moved to the shoulder once the scene was documented.
